themes.summary: Passenger demand remains important, but public industry reporting highlights pressure from higher jet fuel costs and geopolitical route disruption.
themes.key_drivers: Passenger demand; premium travel; cargo; capacity discipline; tourism flows.
themes.key_risks: Fuel prices; airspace disruption; labour costs; recession; regulation.

themes.summary: Clean energy retains strong long-term demand, but offshore wind and renewables developers face interest-rate, supply-chain, and grid-connection pressure.
themes.key_drivers: Decarbonisation; grid investment; electrification; energy security; corporate power demand.
themes.key_risks: Higher rates; permitting delays; supply-chain inflation; policy changes.

themes.summary: Construction demand is supported by infrastructure renewal and energy projects, but rates, labour, and material costs remain headwinds.
themes.key_drivers: Public infrastructure spending; housing cycles; energy infrastructure; urban renewal.
themes.key_risks: Higher rates; cost overruns; weak property markets; public budget constraints.

themes.summary: Copper is supported by power grids, AI data centers, EVs, renewables, and infrastructure, while supply growth remains difficult.
themes.key_drivers: Grid expansion; electrification; AI data-center power needs; EVs; constrained mine supply.
themes.key_risks: China slowdown; mine supply surprises; substitution; global recession.

themes.summary: Gold remains strategically relevant as a hedge, but recent public commentary shows sensitivity to real yields, the US dollar, and investor flows.
themes.key_drivers: Central-bank demand; geopolitical risk; real interest rates; US dollar; ETF flows.
themes.key_risks: Higher bond yields; stronger US dollar; weaker physical demand; crowded positioning.

themes.summary: Healthcare offers defensive long-term demand from ageing populations, chronic disease, and innovation, while pricing and pipeline risks remain central.
themes.key_drivers: Ageing populations; obesity and diabetes demand; oncology; diagnostics; emerging-market access.
themes.key_risks: Drug pricing pressure; trial failures; patent expiries; regulation.

themes.summary: Infrastructure is supported by grid upgrades, transport renewal, energy security, and public investment needs.
themes.key_drivers: Grid bottlenecks; transport investment; energy transition; data centers; public-private partnerships.
themes.key_risks: Regulatory returns; budget pressure; execution risk; higher financing costs.

themes.summary: Diversified mining is supported by electrification and infrastructure demand for industrial metals, while new supply is limited by permitting timelines, grade decline and capital discipline.
themes.key_drivers: Electrification and grid demand; infrastructure spending; ore grades and permitting; capital discipline; China demand.
themes.key_risks: Global growth slowdown; cost inflation in energy and labour; resource nationalism and royalties; operational and safety disruption.

themes.summary: Rare earths remain strategically important for magnets, defence, clean energy, and electronics, with supply-chain concentration a persistent risk.
themes.key_drivers: Permanent magnets; defence demand; EV motors; wind turbines; supply-chain security policy.
themes.key_risks: China policy shifts; opaque pricing; project execution; environmental permitting.

themes.summary: Silver benefits from precious-metal demand and industrial uses, but mine supply and economic sensitivity make it more volatile than gold.
themes.key_drivers: Solar demand; electronics; monetary demand; mine supply; gold/silver ratio.
themes.key_risks: Industrial slowdown; mining cost inflation; sharp risk-off liquidations.

themes.summary: Athletic apparel and sportswear demand is supported by health and leisure trends and by premium brand pricing power, while volume growth is tied to discretionary consumer spending.
themes.key_drivers: Consumer discretionary spending; brand strength and pricing power; health and leisure participation; direct-to-consumer channels; sports sponsorship cycles.
themes.key_risks: Discretionary spending squeeze; inventory and discounting cycles; freight and input costs; fashion risk and brand fatigue.

themes.summary: Steel demand tracks construction and infrastructure activity, with margins driven by the spread between input costs and prices and heavily influenced by trade policy and overcapacity.
themes.key_drivers: Infrastructure and construction spending; iron ore and coking coal costs; tariffs and trade policy; decarbonisation of production; China output.
themes.key_risks: Global overcapacity; construction slowdown; input cost spikes; carbon-cost transition and stranded assets.

themes.summary: Software, cloud and semiconductor demand is underpinned by AI infrastructure build-out and enterprise digitisation, but the sector carries high valuations and is unusually sensitive to interest-rate expectations.
themes.key_drivers: AI infrastructure spending; cloud migration; enterprise software budgets; semiconductor cycle; data-centre capacity.
themes.key_risks: Rate-driven valuation compression; AI capex digestion; export controls and supply chains; concentration in a few large names.

themes.summary: Utilities benefit from electrification and grid demand, but forecasting data-center load and funding network expansion are major challenges.
themes.key_drivers: AI data centers; electrification; grid reinforcement; regulated asset growth; renewable integration.
themes.key_risks: Regulatory pressure; customer bill affordability; capex overruns; interest rates.
